explanation: This is the order of Mark Harris's reduction walk-through (see Sources), and interviewers like it because each step fixes the bottleneck the previous one exposed: divergence, then bank conflicts, then idle threads, then instruction overhead, then too little work per thread. The last step changes the kernel from compute-overhead-bound to bandwidth-bound: most of the summing happens in registers while loads stream in, and only one block-level reduction per block remains. The GPU gym's `reduction` exercise benchmarks each version.
